title: Allowance App Chore-to-Payout Latency
dataSources: Nanit sleep sessions (`nanit:sleep`), Hatch routines (`hatch:routine`), school calendar events (`schoolcalendar:event`), allowance transactions (`allowance:txn`), and kid screen usage (`screentime:usage`).
app: Family-routine telemetry from Nanit sleep exports, Hatch routine data, school calendars, allowance and chore apps, and Apple Screen Time sent to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=allowance:txn
| search event_type="chore_payout" payout_delay_hr=*
| stats avg(payout_delay_hr) as avg_payout_delay_hr perc90(payout_delay_hr) as p90_payout_delay_hr count as samples by child_name
| sort 0 - avg_payout_delay_hr
description: Measures chore payout latency by child. Runs scheduled SPL against `index=personal` to surface **Allowance App Chore-to-Payout Latency** so you can spot drift before it becomes a habit.
value: Slow payout erodes trust in the system, so a simple latency view helps keep the reward loop credible.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for chore payout latency to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 chore payout latency.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Family, Baby & Household Chaos — typical feeds: Baby feeds (`baby:feed`), baby sleep (`baby:sleep`), diaper changes (`diaper:change`), chore completions (`chore:completion`), allowance ledger (`allowance:ledger`), family calendar (`family:calendar`.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `allowance:txn`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=allowance:txn`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Baby-tracking app exports (Huckleberry/Baby Daybook), chore and allowance boards, shared family calendars, screen-time reports, and growth logs via Splunk HEC scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Send the relevant duration field for chore payout latency to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "allowance:txn", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=allowance:txn earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Allowance App Chore-to-Payout Latency** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=allowance:txn`) across the full search range. The `avg, perc90` aggregation groups by `child_name`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `child_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=allowance:txn
| search event_type="chore_payout" payout_delay_hr=*
| stats avg(payout_delay_hr) as avg_payout_delay_hr perc90(payout_delay_hr) as p90_payout_delay_hr count as samples by child_name
| sort 0 - avg_payout_delay_hr
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=allowance:txn earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table child_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=allowance:txn earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.23.25: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Average And P90 Chore Payout Latency (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `allowance:txn` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=allowance:txn | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
